steps.text: Combine milk, pumpkin, sugar, vanilla extract, and cinnamon in a large saucepan over medium heat. Use a whisk to blend well. Heat to a simmer; do not boil.

raw_recipe.headline: Famous No Coffee Pumpkin Latte
raw_recipe.description: This famous no-coffee pumpkin latte recipe makes a creamy, satisfying drink just like that popular coffee house serves, except without the caffeine.
raw_recipe.name: Famous No Coffee Pumpkin Latte

recipeInstructions.text: Combine milk, pumpkin, sugar, vanilla extract, and cinnamon in a large saucepan over medium heat. Use a whisk to blend well. Heat to a simmer; do not boil.

review.reviewBody: My kids and I loved this. Loved. I will admit, I did add coffee to mine, but the kids drank theirs as is and asked for the rest of what was left in the saucepan. A+ drink.

I love this drink! Instead of messing with the stove, I just throw all the ingredients into my Vitamix, and blend on high until it steams. Super easy! I also added 1/2 tbsp coffee extract, and I used vanilla almond milk since I have a dairy intolerance. Fantastic, definitely recommend!

I made it with some changes. Used fresh pumpkin and used the nutri bullet to blend everything together, then simmered to light boil and poured a cup of boiled tetley orange pekoe tea in it, it was amazing, drank half hot and left the rest in refrigerator. to cool and drank later. We just loved it

I loved it. But to make it that much greater I substituted the white sugar for 1/2 cup brown sugar as suggested in one of the reviews and I added 1/2 tsp nutmeg, 1/4 tsp ground cloves and 1/4 tsp fresh grated ginger. I also blended the mixture afterwards. But next time I would use ground ginger instead of fresh grated ginger because even after I blended the mixture there were still a few chunky bits of ginger. This recipe made 1 quart (4 cups). I stored the leftovers in the fridge and sometimes served it cold which tasted just as good. I even mixed it with some hot chocolate to make a pumpkin spice hot chocolate. YUM.

I'm not a super fan of pumpkin lattes, but this is pretty good. I tried it as-is, and it's okay, but then I tried it with 1/2 a quart of coffee (I used Einstein bros. vanilla hazelnut) and 1/2 a quart of half&half. I brewed the coffee just for this, so I mixed the pumpkin, sugar, and spices in my saucepan, then poured the coffee in and mixed it over med. low heat. I think that the heat of the coffee helped to dissolve the pumpkin a little bit. Then I stirred in the half&half. I left it over med. low heat for maybe 5 minutes, then turned it to low and left it there until I could see the steam coming off of it, stirring consistently. I then poured it into a mug and topped it with cool whip and freshly grated nutmeg. De-lish.

A good recipe! I made this two ways - one without the coffee as listed for my kids, and one with coffee for myself. I was really surprised my kids didn't like this - maybe if I had strained it first (they thought it was too pulpy). I'll also try the blender next time, as another reviewer suggested. Now for the coffee version - outstanding!!! Perfect drink for a cool fall day! I used 1/2 cup of brown sugar instead of the 1/4 cup of white (it wasn't too sweet at all, especially considering it was going to be mixed with coffee) and I also added a 1/2 teaspoon of pumpkin pie spice... but this was good without those additions too, it all comes down to personal taste. Then I added a cup of the pumpkin milk mixture to 1 cup of very strong coffee and topped with some whipped cream and a sprinkle of pumpkin pie spice... best pumpkin latte ever! I will definitely be making this again!

Loved this! This is really great to make for a large group - those who prefer it without coffee can drink it as-is, and you can have some strong coffee for others to add as they wish (very good that way). Instead of straight-up cinnamon I used the same amount of a cinnamon + spice blend that included ginger and clove, and it was very good. I love that it uses real pumpkin - definitely healthier than the coffee house version of this drink!

EDITED TO ADD: The second time I made it, I used a blender to avoid the bottom of the pot being 'thick'. This worked REALLY well. Throw it in cold (before adding sugar), then heat on stove and add sugar. You could also blend it hot, particularly if you have an immersion hand mixer (which I do not). This made a HUGE difference in the texture.

This drink is delicious! Thick, rich, and creamy and oh so pleasantly pumpkin. I believe the success to making this recipe five stars is in the quality of the pumpkin you use. I used puree that I made myself from a sugar pumpkin and it was naturally sweet and the consistency of baby food. Perhaps using baby food, if you can find pumpkin, would yield better results because mine disintegrated well in the warm milk. I used brown sugar instead of white and used pumpkin pie spice instead of cinnamon because I wanted it spicier. I heated all the ingredients stovetop and before serving blended it with a stick blender which made a thick latte-like frothy topping and distributed the spice well through out the drink. This is one of those drinks ideal to nestle down on the couch with to settle in for the night. Sweet enough to feel indulgent but not with a sugar load that you regret. Thanks RESCUERANGER, this one is going on an index card clipped to the fridge as I know I'll be making it a lot!
This drink is extremely good, but make sure to be generous with the cinnamon! Other than that, cook the drink a few minutes longer (11-13 minutes) to make sure that the liquid can blend a lot better.

This is pretty good! Almost as good as Panera's (theirs is a little more creamy). I used 2% milk (I just microwaved it), mixed in some ground nutmeg and ground cloves like some reviewers did, used Splenda, and I didn't measure the vanilla- I always put more than stated on the recipe. I also added a little more pumpkin purée since the texture seemed thin. Next time I'll try adding instant coffee to the milk because milk alone makes me too sleepy.

I didn't want a large qty of this, so made a single serving with 1/4 c pumpkin puree (canned), 3/4 C milk, 2 t sugar, 1/2 t pumpkin pie spice and 1/2 t vanilla. Turned out great! Was a little more 'texture' than I wanted, but the flavor was wonderful and I think others suggested straining it to get a smoother texture and I am sure that would make a very smooth result. I have tried pumpkin latte recipes before, this is the best so far! p.s. -- I "had" to add a shot of espresso to mine... coffee lover here! - without the shot, I'd maybe increase the milk to 1 C for a single serving.
Tastes absolutely delicious, takes only a few minutes, and it really soothes the part of me that craves a pumpkin spice latte but can't have coffee.
Love with whipped cream and cinnamon on top!

My 11 year old made this, and he added probably 2 cups of pumpkin purée from a pumpkin he picked from our garden. He put some homemade whip cream on top and he loved it! P.S. he also modified the ingredients a little bit. He used maple syrup instead of sugar and almond milk instead of milk.

I love this recipe and so does my family! I make it every fall. I usually add ground cardamom and cloves to make it more like a chai pumpkin drink. Question for anyone out there: I’m throwing a fall party and would like to add some rum. Has anyone tried that? How does that taste? Does it enhance or ruin the flavor? Any other types of alcohol anyone would recommend?

This was pretty okay. The puree gives the drink a weird texture though- thick and a little grainy as the puree particles float around in each sip but mostly sit at the bottom. I think I would have liked it to be sweeter, so maybe if you have a sweet tooth like me, add a little more sugar or maybe vanilla syrup instead of vanilla extract plus the sugar that the recipe calls for. I also used pumpkin spice instead of cinnamon since I really like the pumpkin flavor. I will finish up the leftover drink I have but won't make it again.
It was ok, I followed the recipe and it just tasted like milk. Also, the cinnamon just floats to the top.
almost better than a real pumpkin spice latte!
I loved this drink! I had absolutely no problems with it. It's super easy to make.
It was very good
